claim: Cold exposure triggers neogenesis in classic interscapular brown adipose tissue (iBAT) that involves activation of β1-adrenergic receptors.
source: Cold exposure triggers neogenesis in classic interscapular brown adipose tissue (iBAT) that involves activation of β1-adrenergic receptors, proliferation of PDGFRA+ adipose tissue stromal cells (ASCs), and recruitment of immune cells whose phenotypes are presently unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known phenomenon that the study investigates.

claim: Cold exposure triggers proliferation of PDGFRA+ adipose tissue stromal cells (ASCs).
source: Cold exposure triggers neogenesis in classic interscapular brown adipose tissue (iBAT) that involves activation of β1-adrenergic receptors, proliferation of PDGFRA+ adipose tissue stromal cells (ASCs), and recruitment of immune cells whose phenotypes are presently unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known phenomenon.

claim: Cold exposure triggers recruitment of immune cells to iBAT.
source: Cold exposure triggers neogenesis in classic interscapular brown adipose tissue (iBAT) that involves activation of β1-adrenergic receptors, proliferation of PDGFRA+ adipose tissue stromal cells (ASCs), and recruitment of immune cells whose phenotypes are presently unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known phenomenon.

claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing identified three ASC subpopulations that occupied distinct tissue locations.
source: Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) in mice identified three ASC subpopulations that occupied distinct tissue locations.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the scRNA-seq experiments reported in the study.

claim: Interstitial ASC1 are direct precursors of new brown adipocytes.
source: Of these, interstitial ASC1 were found to be direct precursors of new brown adipocytes (BAs).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's scRNA-seq and fate mapping experiments.

claim: Knockout of β1-adrenergic receptors in ASCs did not prevent cold-induced neogenesis.
source: Surprisingly, knockout of β1-adrenergic receptors in ASCs did not prevent cold-induced neogenesis, whereas pharmacological activation of the β3-adrenergic receptor on BAs was sufficient, suggesting that signals derived from mature BAs indirectly trigger ASC proliferation and differentiation.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the Adrb1 knockout experiments.

claim: Pharmacological activation of the β3-adrenergic receptor on BAs is sufficient to induce neogenesis.
source: Surprisingly, knockout of β1-adrenergic receptors in ASCs did not prevent cold-induced neogenesis, whereas pharmacological activation of the β3-adrenergic receptor on BAs was sufficient, suggesting that signals derived from mature BAs indirectly trigger ASC proliferation and differentiation.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the CL316,243 treatment experiments.

claim: Signals derived from mature brown adipocytes indirectly trigger ASC proliferation and differentiation.
source: Surprisingly, knockout of β1-adrenergic receptors in ASCs did not prevent cold-induced neogenesis, whereas pharmacological activation of the β3-adrenergic receptor on BAs was sufficient, suggesting that signals derived from mature BAs indirectly trigger ASC proliferation and differentiation.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental findings from the Adrb1 KO and ADRB3 agonist experiments.

claim: Cold exposure induced the delayed appearance of multiple macrophage and dendritic cell populations.
source: In this regard, cold exposure induced the delayed appearance of multiple macrophage and dendritic cell populations whose recruitment strongly correlated with the onset and magnitude of neogenesis across diverse experimental conditions.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the scRNA-seq analysis of immune cells.

claim: Recruitment of macrophage and dendritic cell populations strongly correlated with the onset and magnitude of neogenesis across diverse experimental conditions.
source: In this regard, cold exposure induced the delayed appearance of multiple macrophage and dendritic cell populations whose recruitment strongly correlated with the onset and magnitude of neogenesis across diverse experimental conditions.
evidence: This is a primary finding from correlation analysis across multiple experimental conditions.

claim: Cold-induced neogenesis involves dynamic interactions between ASC1 and recruited immune cells that occur on the micrometer scale in distinct tissue regions.
source: High-resolution immunofluorescence and single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization demonstrated that cold-induced neogenesis involves dynamic interactions between ASC1 and recruited immune cells that occur on the micrometer scale in distinct tissue regions.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the immunofluorescence and smFISH experiments.

claim: Neogenesis is not a reflexive response of progenitors to β-adrenergic signaling.
source: Our results indicate that neogenesis is not a reflexive response of progenitors to β-adrenergic signaling, but rather is a complex adaptive response to elevated metabolic demand within brown adipocytes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings, particularly the Adrb1 KO experiments.

claim: Neogenesis is a complex adaptive response to elevated metabolic demand within brown adipocytes.
source: Our results indicate that neogenesis is not a reflexive response of progenitors to β-adrenergic signaling, but rather is a complex adaptive response to elevated metabolic demand within brown adipocytes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Brown adipose tissue is a specialized organ that is the dominant site of non-shivering thermogenesis in neonatal mammals.
source: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) is a specialized organ that is the dominant site of non-shivering thermogenesis in neonatal mammals (Dawkins and Hull, 1964).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Dawkins and Hull, 1964.

claim: Adult mammals, including humans, have metabolically active BAT.
source: While critical for regulation of neonatal body temperature, adult mammals, including humans, also have metabolically active BAT (Cypess et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2013b; Sacks and Symonds, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cypess et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2013b; Sacks and Symonds, 2013.

claim: Adult BAT mass and function are associated with a healthier metabolic profile in both rodents and humans.
source: Importantly, adult BAT mass and function are associated with a healthier metabolic profile in both rodents and humans (Becher et al., 2021; Wibmer et al., 2021; Herz et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Becher et al., 2021; Wibmer et al., 2021; Herz et al., 2021.

claim: BAT abundance and activity is associated with higher energy expenditure.
source: Although the direct mechanisms have not been fully elucidated, BAT abundance and activity is associated with higher energy expenditure, altered secretion of hormones (Chondronikola et al., 2016; Géloën et al., 1988; Hanssen et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2015; Villarroya et al., 2017; Villarroya et al., 2019), and reduced visceral fat mass (Herz et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: BAT abundance and activity is associated with altered secretion of hormones.
source: Although the direct mechanisms have not been fully elucidated, BAT abundance and activity is associated with higher energy expenditure, altered secretion of hormones (Chondronikola et al., 2016; Géloën et al., 1988; Hanssen et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2015; Villarroya et al., 2017; Villarroya et al., 2019), and reduced visceral fat mass (Herz et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chondronikola et al., 2016; Géloën et al., 1988; Hanssen et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2015; Villarroya et al., 2017; Villarroya et al., 2019.

claim: BAT abundance and activity is associated with reduced visceral fat mass.
source: Although the direct mechanisms have not been fully elucidated, BAT abundance and activity is associated with higher energy expenditure, altered secretion of hormones (Chondronikola et al., 2016; Géloën et al., 1988; Hanssen et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2015; Villarroya et al., 2017; Villarroya et al., 2019), and reduced visceral fat mass (Herz et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Herz et al., 2021.

claim: Cold exposure triggers BAT neogenesis in rodents.
source: Cold exposure triggers BAT neogenesis and is an important adaptive means to increase the capacity for non-shivering thermogenesis in rodents (Bukowiecki et al., 1982; Bukowiecki et al., 1986; Foster and Frydman, 1978; Nedergaard, 1982; Nedergaard et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bukowiecki et al., 1982; Bukowiecki et al., 1986; Foster and Frydman, 1978; Nedergaard, 1982; Nedergaard et al., 2019.

claim: Fate mapping studies in rats indicated that brown adipocytes arise from interstitial cells that proliferate and differentiate during the first few days of cold exposure.
source: Fate mapping studies in rats by Bukowiecki et al. strongly indicated that brown adipocytes (BAs) arise from interstitial cells that proliferate and differentiate during the first few days of cold exposure (Bukowiecki et al., 1986; Géloën et al., 1988).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bukowiecki et al., 1986; Géloën et al., 1988.

claim: Most, if not all, BAs induced by cold arise from stromal cells that express PDGFRA.
source: More recently, genetic lineage-tracing experiments from our lab demonstrated that most, if not all, BAs induced by cold arise from stromal cells that express the surface marker platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha (PDGFRA).
evidence: This is based on genetic lineage-tracing experiments from the authors' lab.

claim: Cold exposure remodels the vasculature in BAT.
source: In addition to effects on brown adipogenesis, cold exposure also remodels the vasculature, recruits monocytes/macrophages, and triggers proliferation of uncharacterized population(s) of cells that are potentially important for proper BAT expansion and remodeling (Lee et al., 2015; Géloën et al., 1988).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2015; Géloën et al., 1988.

claim: Cold exposure recruits monocytes/macrophages to BAT.
source: In addition to effects on brown adipogenesis, cold exposure also remodels the vasculature, recruits monocytes/macrophages, and triggers proliferation of uncharacterized population(s) of cells that are potentially important for proper BAT expansion and remodeling (Lee et al., 2015; Géloën et al., 1988).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2015; Géloën et al., 1988.

claim: Recent single-cell transcriptional analysis indicates the existence of multiple stromal cell types in white adipose tissue depots that express PDGFRA.
source: In this regard, recent single-cell transcriptional analysis indicates the existence of multiple stromal cell types in white adipose tissue (WAT) depots that express PDGFRA (Burl et al., 2018; Hepler et al., 2018; Merrick et al., 2019; Schwalie et al., 2018; Emont et al., 2022; Rondini and Granneman, 2020; Sárvári et al., 2021; Rondini et al., 2021), and that recruitment of brown/beige adipocytes in response to β3-adrenergic activation involves specific subsets of stromal cells and immune cells.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Burl et al., 2018; Hepler et al., 2018; Merrick et al., 2019; Schwalie et al., 2018; Emont et al., 2022; Rondini and Granneman, 2020; Sárvári et al., 2021; Rondini et al., 2021.

claim: Recruitment of brown/beige adipocytes in response to β3-adrenergic activation involves specific subsets of stromal cells and immune cells.
source: In this regard, recent single-cell transcriptional analysis indicates the existence of multiple stromal cell types in white adipose tissue (WAT) depots that express PDGFRA (Burl et al., 2018; Hepler et al., 2018; Merrick et al., 2019; Schwalie et al., 2018; Emont et al., 2022; Rondini and Granneman, 2020; Sárvári et al., 2021; Rondini et al., 2021), and that recruitment of brown/beige adipocytes in response to β3-adrenergic activation involves specific subsets of stromal cells and immune cells.
evidence: This is supported by the cited single-cell transcriptional analysis studies.

claim: Cold triggers proliferation of cells expressing the myeloid cell surface marker F4/80.
source: In addition, we previously observed that cold triggers proliferation of cells expressing the myeloid cell surface marker F4/80, as well as uncharacterized population(s) of stromal cells (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claim: Cold-induced mitogenesis in rodent BAT only commences after more than 2 days of cold exposure.
source: Curiously, cold-induced mitogenesis in rodent BAT only commences after more than 2 days of cold exposure (Bukowiecki et al., 1982; Bukowiecki et al., 1986; Hunt and Hunt, 1967; Lee et al., 2015) and is concentrated within specific regions of the tissue (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bukowiecki et al., 1982; Bukowiecki et al., 1986; Hunt and Hunt, 1967; Lee et al., 2015.

claim: Cold-induced mitogenesis is concentrated within specific regions of the tissue.
source: Curiously, cold-induced mitogenesis in rodent BAT only commences after more than 2 days of cold exposure (Bukowiecki et al., 1982; Bukowiecki et al., 1986; Hunt and Hunt, 1967; Lee et al., 2015) and is concentrated within specific regions of the tissue (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claim: Cold-induced neogenesis in BAT requires intact sympathetic activity.
source: Cold-induced neogenesis in BAT requires intact sympathetic activity that can be mimicked by systemic norepinephrine (NE) infusion in warm-adapted mice (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claim: Systemic norepinephrine infusion can mimic cold-induced neogenesis in warm-adapted mice.
source: Cold-induced neogenesis in BAT requires intact sympathetic activity that can be mimicked by systemic norepinephrine (NE) infusion in warm-adapted mice (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claim: The effects of NE infusion are prevented by global knockout of ADRB1.
source: Moreover, the effects of NE infusion are prevented by global knockout (KO) of the β1-adrenergic receptor (ADRB1) (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claim: ADRB1, but not ADRB3, are present on ASC.
source: ADRB1, but not β3-adrenergic receptors (ADRB3), are present on ASC, and in vitro experiments suggested that activation of preadipocyte ADRB1 mediates cold-induced BA neogenesis (Bronnikov et al., 1999; Bronnikov et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bronnikov et al., 1999; Bronnikov et al., 1992.

claim: In vitro experiments suggested that activation of preadipocyte ADRB1 mediates cold-induced BA neogenesis.
source: ADRB1, but not β3-adrenergic receptors (ADRB3), are present on ASC, and in vitro experiments suggested that activation of preadipocyte ADRB1 mediates cold-induced BA neogenesis (Bronnikov et al., 1999; Bronnikov et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bronnikov et al., 1999; Bronnikov et al., 1992.

claim: K-means clustering of the top differentially expressed genes identified three distinct patterns of upregulated gene expression during cold exposure.
source: K-means clustering of the top differentially expressed genes (DEGs) identified three distinct patterns of upregulated gene expression (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Acutely upregulated genes were induced within 6 hours of cold exposure, but then returned to control levels after chronic cold acclimation.
source: Acutely upregulated genes were induced within 6 hours of cold exposure, but then returned to control levels after chronic cold acclimation.
evidence: This is a finding from the RNA-seq time course analysis.

claim: Acutely upregulated genes include Ppargc1a, Ucp1, Nr4a1, and Dio2.
source: Genes in this cluster are well-known targets of protein kinase A (PKA), including peroxisome proliferative activated receptor gamma coactivator 1 alpha (Ppargc1a), uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1), nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 1 (Nr4a1), and iodothyronine deiodinase 2 (Dio2) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Chronically upregulated genes were induced following 1–2 days of cold exposure and remained elevated for the duration of the time in cold.
source: Chronically upregulated genes were induced following 1–2 days of cold exposure and remained elevated for the duration of the time in cold.
evidence: This is a finding from the RNA-seq time course analysis.

claim: Chronically upregulated genes include Elovl3, Fasn, and Pdk4.
source: This cluster included genes involved in lipid synthesis and oxidation, such as elongation of very long chain fatty acids-like 3 (Elovl3), fatty acid synthase (Fasn), and pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase isoenzyme 4 (Pdk4).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNA-seq analysis.

claim: The third cluster of genes showed delayed and variable upregulation among individual mice.
source: The third cluster was interesting, as the gene upregulation was delayed and variable among individual mice.
evidence: This is a finding from the RNA-seq time course analysis.

claim: The third cluster of genes included proliferation markers (Birc5, Top2a) and genes indicating innate immune activation and macrophage recruitment (Lgals3, Gpnmb, Trem2).
source: Genes in this cluster included proliferation markers (Birc5, Top2a), as well as various genes indicating innate immune activation and macrophage recruitment (Lgals3, Gpnmb, Trem2) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Proliferation markers and immune cell recruitment markers were highly correlated and this relationship was largely independent of time spent in the cold.
source: Importantly, these variables were highly correlated and this relationship was largely independent of time spent in the cold (Figure 1B; p<0.001).
evidence: This is a finding from correlation analysis of the RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Cell proliferation and immune cell recruitment peak around the fourth day of cold exposure.
source: These data confirm that cell proliferation and immune cell recruitment are connected and peak around the fourth day of cold exposure.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the RNA-seq time course data.

claim: Lineage marker negative (Lin-) cell libraries contained adipose stromal cells (Pdgfra+ ASCs), vascular cells, and proliferating/newly differentiating adipocytes.
source: Lineage marker negative (Lin-) cell libraries contained adipose stromal cells (Pdgfra+ ASCs), vascular cells, and proliferating/newly differentiating adipocytes (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Clustering of scRNA-seq data from control and cold-exposed mice identified eight major clusters.
source: Clustering of scRNA-seq data from control and cold-exposed mice identified eight major clusters, ranging from ~500 to 6,500 cells per cluster (Figure 2A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Three clusters were defined as ASCs based on their expression of Pdgfra, Cd34, and Ly6a.
source: Three of these clusters were defined as ASCs based on their expression of common mesenchymal stem cell markers Pdgfra, Cd34, and lymphocyte antigen 6 complex locus A (Ly6a, a.k.a. Sca1) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A) that are often used for identification of adipocyte progenitors (Burl et al., 2018; Hepler et al., 2018; Merrick et al., 2019; Schwalie et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis with support from cited literature.

claim: Two cell clusters were unique to cold-exposed mice.
source: Separating data by treatment revealed that two cell clusters were unique to cold-exposed mice (circled; Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: One cold-unique cluster retained numerous ASC markers like Pdgfra.
source: One cluster retained numerous ASC markers like Pdgfra, whereas the other was largely Pdgfra negative and expressed high levels of markers of proliferation (e.g. Birc5) and adipocyte differentiation (e.g. Car3) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: One cold-unique cluster was largely Pdgfra negative and expressed high levels of markers of proliferation and adipocyte differentiation.
source: One cluster retained numerous ASC markers like Pdgfra, whereas the other was largely Pdgfra negative and expressed high levels of markers of proliferation (e.g. Birc5) and adipocyte differentiation (e.g. Car3) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: High-resolution clustering resolved three distinct ASC cell types prominent in iBAT controls: ASC1-3.
source: This clustering resolved three distinct ASC cell types prominent in iBAT controls: ASC1-3 (Figure 2C, left).
evidence: This is a finding from the high-resolution scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: ASC1 selectively expressed Col5a3, Cxcl14, and Bmper.
source: Thus, ASC1 selectively expressed collagen type V alpha 3 chain (Col5a3), C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 14 (Cxcl14), and the bone morphogenic protein (BMP)-binding endothelial regulator (Bmper) (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: ASC2 cells expressed Pi16, Dpp4, and Fbn1.
source: Cells in ASC2 expressed secreted protease inhibitor peptidase inhibitor 16 (Pi16), surface glycoprotein dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (Dpp4), and the ECM component fibronectin (Fbn1).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: ASC3 cells selectively expressed Gdf10, Clec11a, and Fbln1.
source: ASC3 cells selectively expressed secreted ligand growth differentiation factor 10 (Gdf10), C-type lectin domain containing 11a (Clec11a), and fibulin1 (Fbln1) (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: High-resolution clustering identified three additional cell clusters in cold-exposed mice.
source: High-resolution clustering identified three additional cell clusters in cold-exposed mice (Figure 2C, right).
evidence: This is a finding from the high-resolution scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: All three additional cold-induced clusters expressed ASC1-specific markers.
source: All of these clusters expressed ASC1-specific markers; however, two of the clusters were primarily defined by genes for proliferation (Top2a, Birc5, Stmn1), and/or adipogenic differentiation (Pparg, Lpl, Nnat) (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Cold exposure greatly reduced expression of genes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis, cell adhesion, and extracellular matrix organization in ASC1.
source: Examination of the two ASC1 expression states indicated that cold activation greatly reduced expression of genes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis (sterol biosynthetic process; GO:0016126, p=2.8E-10), cell adhesion (GO:0007155, p=4.9E-2) and extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198, p=7.7E-7), and strongly induced expression of genes involved in immune system process (GO:0002376, p=2.2E-6), chemokine activity (GO:0008009, p=5.0E-3) and cell migration (GO:0016477, p=3.6E-4).
evidence: This is a finding from Gene Ontology analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: Cold exposure strongly induced expression of genes involved in immune system process, chemokine activity, and cell migration in ASC1.
source: Examination of the two ASC1 expression states indicated that cold activation greatly reduced expression of genes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis (sterol biosynthetic process; GO:0016126, p=2.8E-10), cell adhesion (GO:0007155, p=4.9E-2) and extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198, p=7.7E-7), and strongly induced expression of genes involved in immune system process (GO:0002376, p=2.2E-6), chemokine activity (GO:0008009, p=5.0E-3) and cell migration (GO:0016477, p=3.6E-4).
evidence: This is a finding from Gene Ontology analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: ASC1 cells expressed higher levels of Pparg and its target genes, such as Lpl.
source: In addition, ASC1 cells appeared highly poised for adipogenesis, expressing higher levels of the master adipocyte transcriptional regulator peroxisome proliferator activated receptor gamma (Pparg) and its target genes, such as lipoprotein lipase (Lpl) (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Cells in the differentiating cluster selectively expressed Nnat that was transiently upregulated during differentiation and silenced in mature BAs.
source: Notably, cells in the differentiating cluster selectively expressed the imprinted gene neuronatin (Nnat) that was transiently upregulated during differentiation and silenced in mature BAs (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Numerous ASC1-specific marker genes were co-expressed in the proliferating and differentiating clusters.
source: Numerous ASC1-specific marker genes were co-expressed in the proliferating and differentiating clusters (Figure 2D), indicating that expression of these genes persists as cell differentiated into BAs.
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: None of the ASC2 and ASC3 markers were expressed in the proliferating/differentiating clusters.
source: In contrast, none of the aforementioned ASC2 and ASC3 markers were expressed in these proliferating/differentiating clusters (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Cold-activated ASC1 are the immediate progenitors of new BAs induced by cold exposure.
source: From these data, we concluded that cold-activated ASC1 are the immediate progenitors of new BAs induced by cold exposure.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the scRNA-seq data.

claim: Differentiating cells exhibited a clear trajectory along t-SNE2 that included loss of Pdgfra expression, transient proliferation (Birc5), and sequential upregulation of early (Cebpa) and late (Adipoq, Ucp1) markers of brown adipogenesis.
source: In addition, differentiating cells exhibited a clear trajectory along t-SNE2 that included loss of ASC marker expression (Pdgfra), transient proliferation (Birc5), and sequential upregulation of early (Cebpa) and late (Adipoq, Ucp1) markers of brown adipogenesis (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Proliferating, non-differentiating cells that retained ASC1 marker expression did not appear to contribute to adipogenesis and might function to replenish the ASC1 population.
source: In contrast, the proliferating, non-differentiating cells that retained ASC1 marker expression did not appear to contribute to adipogenesis and might function to replenish the ASC1 population, as suggested by previous fate mapping studies (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the scRNA-seq data and previous fate mapping studies.

claim: Interstitial ASC1 cells are highly responsive to cold exposure and comprise most, if not all, BA progenitors during acute cold-induced neogenesis.
source: In summary, analysis of BAT ASCs and total stromal cell populations indicates that interstitial ASC1 cells are highly responsive to cold exposure and comprise most, if not all, BA progenitors during acute cold-induced neogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the scRNA-seq and spatial analysis data.

claim: ASC1 comprised the majority of the PDGFRA+ parenchymal interstitial cells.
source: Using smFISH, we found that while ASC1 comprised the majority of the PDGFRA+ parenchymal interstitial cells, ASC2 were localized to the tissue fascia and surrounding large vessels, whereas ASC3 were predominately localized to areas surrounding vessels, but not capillaries (Figure 3B–C).
evidence: This is a finding from the smFISH analysis shown in Figure 3B–C.

claim: ASC2 were localized to the tissue fascia and surrounding large vessels.
source: Using smFISH, we found that while ASC1 comprised the majority of the PDGFRA+ parenchymal interstitial cells, ASC2 were localized to the tissue fascia and surrounding large vessels, whereas ASC3 were predominately localized to areas surrounding vessels, but not capillaries (Figure 3B–C).
evidence: This is a finding from the smFISH analysis shown in Figure 3B–C.

claim: ASC3 were predominately localized to areas surrounding vessels, but not capillaries.
source: Using smFISH, we found that while ASC1 comprised the majority of the PDGFRA+ parenchymal interstitial cells, ASC2 were localized to the tissue fascia and surrounding large vessels, whereas ASC3 were predominately localized to areas surrounding vessels, but not capillaries (Figure 3B–C).
evidence: This is a finding from the smFISH analysis shown in Figure 3B–C.

claim: The interstitial location of ASC1 is consistent with the work of Bukowiecki et al., 1986 who concluded that cold-induced brown adipocytes are derived from interstitial stromal cells.
source: Importantly, the interstitial location of ASC1 is consistent with the work of Bukowiecki et al., 1986 who, using electron microscopy, concluded that cold-induced brown adipocytes are derived from interstitial stromal cells.
evidence: This is a comparison of the current findings with previous work cited.

claim: Nnat expression marks the transient state of early differentiation.
source: Among genes expressed within the adipogenic trajectory, we found that Nnat was induced during early differentiation, then silenced upon terminal differentiation (Figure 4A). Thus, Nnat expression marks the transient state of early differentiation.
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Cold exposure triggered the appearance of numerous Top2a+ Dcn+ cells and clusters of Nnat positive cells.
source: In contrast, cold exposure triggered the appearance of numerous Top2a+ Dcn+ cells, as well as clusters of Nnat positive cells with and without co-expression of Top2a (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from the smFISH analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: High-resolution three-dimensional confocal imaging provided strong evidence for an adipogenic trajectory within a tissue niche.
source: High-resolution three-dimensional confocal imaging provided strong evidence for an adipogenic trajectory within a tissue niche.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the confocal imaging data.

claim: Proliferating ASC1 were observed immediately adjacent to proliferating/differentiating ASC1, and more distally to differentiating ASC1 lacking expression of proliferation markers.
source: Thus, we observed proliferating ASC1 immediately adjacent to proliferating/differentiating ASC1, and more distally to differentiating ASC1 lacking expression of proliferation markers.
evidence: This is a finding from the high-resolution confocal imaging.

claim: The majority of Nnat+ cells co-expressed the ASC1 marker Bmper, but not the ASC2 marker Pi16.
source: As anticipated from scRNA-seq data, the majority of Nnat+ cells co-expressed the ASC1 marker Bmper, but not the ASC2 marker Pi16 (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the smFISH analysis shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Tamoxifen treatment reduced Adrb1 expression in ASC1 by more than 90%.
source: Tamoxifen treatment reduced Adrb1 expression in ASC1 by more than 90% (chi-square p<0.00001, Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis of Adrb1 KO mice shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Knockdown of Adrb1 in ASC1 had no discernable effect on the ability of cold exposure to increase ASC1 proliferation/differentiation.
source: Surprisingly, we found that knockdown of Adrb1 in ASC1 had no discernable effect on the ability of cold exposure to increase ASC1 proliferation/differentiation (both being ~10 fold over basal in WT and Adrb1 KO mice) (Table 1, Supplementary file 4, and Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the Adrb1 KO experiments shown in Table 1 and Figure 5C.

claim: Adrb1 knockout in ASCs had no significant effect on cold-induced expression of proliferation markers at the whole tissue level.
source: In a larger independent cohort of mice, we found that Adrb1 knockout in ASCs had no significant effect on cold-induced expression of proliferation makers at the whole tissue level (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a finding from the qPCR analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Cold induced the appearance of differentiating Nnat+ preadipocytes in the absence of detectible Adrb1 mRNA following Pdgfra-CreERT2-mediated recombination.
source: In addition, smFISH demonstrated that cold induced the appearance of differentiating Nnat+ preadipocytes in the absence of detectible Adrb1 mRNA following Pdgfra-CreERT2-mediated recombination (p<0.00001; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This is a finding from the smFISH analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: ASC Adrb1 expression is not required for cold-induced BA neogenesis.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that ASC Adrb1 expression is not required for cold-induced BA neogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Adrb1 KO experiments.

claim: 68–72% of the total individual variation in proliferation marker expression across treatment groups was accounted for by variation in markers of immune cell recruitment.
source: However, while Adrb1 expression did not impact neogenesis, 68–72% of the total individual variation in proliferation marker expression (Birc5, Top2a) across treatment groups was accounted for by variation in markers of immune cell recruitment (Trem2, Gpnmb; Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a finding from correlation analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: BAs express ADRB1 and, owing to its higher affinity for NE, is a major receptor for mediating cold-induced metabolic activation.
source: BAs also express ADRB1 and, owing to its higher affinity for NE, is a major receptor for mediating cold-induced metabolic activation (Bukowiecki et al., 1978; Chaudhry and Granneman, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bukowiecki et al., 1978; Chaudhry and Granneman, 1999.

claim: CL treatment triggered significant activation, proliferation and differentiation of ASC1 cells.
source: We found that CL treatment triggered significant activation, proliferation and differentiation of ASC1 cells (Table 1, Supplementary file 5, Supplementary file 6, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-F).
evidence: This is a finding from the CL treatment experiments shown in Table 1 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-F.

claim: Cold exposure triggers progenitor proliferation/differentiation indirectly via adrenergic activation of BAs and not through direct ADRB1 activation of progenitors.
source: Taken together, these data strongly suggest that cold exposure triggers progenitor proliferation/differentiation indirectly via adrenergic activation of BAs and not through direct ADRB1 activation of progenitors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Adrb1 KO and CL treatment experiments.

claim: scRNA-seq identified 16 immune clusters in lineage positive (Lin+) cells from mice at RT or exposed to cold.
source: To gain insight into the immune cell complexity of mouse iBAT, we used scRNA-seq to profile lineage positive (Lin+) cells from mice at RT or exposed to cold and identified 16 immune clusters (Figure 6A and Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Seven immune clusters were different subpopulations of macrophages and dendritic cells, comprising 52.0% of the cells in the Lin+ dataset.
source: Seven of these clusters were different subpopulations of macrophages and dendritic cells (MAC and DEND, respectively), comprising 52.0% of the cells in this dataset.
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: Cold exposure dramatically altered the immune cell landscape in mouse iBAT and led to the expansion of dendritic cells and altered phenotype/subtypes of macrophages.
source: Cold exposure dramatically altered the immune cell landscape in mouse iBAT and led to the expansion of dendritic cells and altered phenotype/subtypes of macrophages (Figure 6B, circled).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: All four dendritic cell clusters increased with cold exposure.
source: All four dendritic cell clusters increased with cold exposure (DEND1-4; Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: DEND1 cells expressed conventional dendritic cell type 1 (cDC1) markers, including high levels of Irf8, Ppt1, Jaml, and Naaa.
source: DEND1 cells expressed conventional dendritic cell type 1 (cDC1) markers, including high levels of the master transcriptional regulator Irf8, as well as genes Ppt1, Jaml, and Naaa (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A; Guilliams and van de Laar, 2015; Hilligan and Ronchese, 2020).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, with support from cited literature.

claim: DEND2 were identified as monocyte-derived dendritic cells (moDCs) based on expression of Cd209a and Itgam.
source: We identified the cluster DEND2 as monocyte-derived dendritic cells (moDCs) based on expression of the moDC markers Cd209a and Itgam (CD11b) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A; Cheong et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, with support from cited literature.

claim: moDCs also expressed Tnip3 and Clec4b1.
source: The most abundant dendritic cell type in this dataset (51.6% of dendritic cells), moDCs also expressed Tnip3 and Clec4b1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: DEND3 exhibited profiles consistent with mature/migratory dendritic cells (Tmem123, Ccr7).
source: The minor dendritic cells clusters, DEND3 (12.1%) and DEND4 (2.7%) exhibited profiles consistent with mature/migratory dendritic cells (Tmem123, Ccr7) (Förster et al., 2008; Takekoshi et al., 2010), and plasmacytoid dendritic cells (Irf8 high, Cd7, Tcf4) (Rodrigues et al., 2018; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), respectively.
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, with support from cited literature.

claim: DEND4 exhibited profiles consistent with plasmacytoid dendritic cells (Irf8 high, Cd7, Tcf4).
source: The minor dendritic cells clusters, DEND3 (12.1%) and DEND4 (2.7%) exhibited profiles consistent with mature/migratory dendritic cells (Tmem123, Ccr7) (Förster et al., 2008; Takekoshi et al., 2010), and plasmacytoid dendritic cells (Irf8 high, Cd7, Tcf4) (Rodrigues et al., 2018; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), respectively.
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, with support from cited literature.

claim: Cold-induced proliferation occurs mostly in cDC1 (DEND1) and moDC (DEND2) subpopulations and not in cold-recruited macrophages.
source: While Adgre1 (gene encoding the F4/80 antigen) was expressed in both macrophage and dendritic cell populations (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), multidimensional scRNA-seq analysis indicates cold-induced proliferation occurs mostly in cDC1 (DEND1) and moDC (DEND2) subpopulations and not in cold-recruited macrophages (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: Cold exposure increased the number of MAC1 and MAC3 macrophage populations and reduced the number of MAC2 cells.
source: Cold exposure increased the number of MAC1 and MAC3 macrophage populations and reduced the number of MAC2 cells (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: MAC2 cluster had a resident macrophage profile, and expressed genes including Folr2, F13a1, Cbr2, Pf4, Gas6, and Mrc1.
source: The MAC2 cluster had a resident macrophage profile, and expressed genes including Folr2, F13a1, Cbr2, Pf4, Gas6, and Mrc1.
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: MAC1 cells had an anti-inflammatory and lipid-handling phenotype.
source: The largest cold-induced macrophage cluster, MAC1, had an anti-inflammatory and lipid-handling phenotype.
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: MAC1 cells express Trem2, which functions to promote efferocytosis.
source: MAC1 cells express the dead cell receptor Trem2, which functions to promote efferocytosis (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: MAC1 cells express the anti-inflammatory gene Gpnmb and Spp1, which is known in other adipose depots as chemotactic for ASCs.
source: These cells also express the anti-inflammatory gene Gpnmb, and Spp1, which is known in other adipose depots as chemotactic for ASCs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The top DEGs for MAC1 include genes involved in ECM remodeling (Ctsb, Ctsd, Ctsl, Mmp12), and lipid handling (Fabp5, Lpl, Plin2).
source: Apart from these markers, the top DEGs for MAC1 include genes involved in ECM remodeling (Ctsb, Ctsd, Ctsl, Mmp12), and lipid handling (Fabp5, Lpl, Plin2).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: MAC1 macrophages have a similar expression profile to that recently described during WAT remodeling.
source: These macrophages have a similar expression profile to that recently described during WAT remodeling (Burl et al., 2018; Jaitin et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous studies cited.

claim: MAC3 had lower expression of MAC1 markers and higher expression of interferon-activated genes.
source: The second cold-induced macrophage cluster, MAC3, had lower expression of these MAC1 markers and higher expression of interferon-activated genes (Ifi204, Ifi207, Ifi209), several c-type lectin domain family 4 members (Clec4d, Clec4e, Clec4n), and many other interferon-regulated genes (Irf7, Slfn2, Ifit3, Rsad2, Isg15).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: ASC1 proliferation and differentiation were strongly predicted by the magnitude of cold-induced recruitment of cDC1 (DEND1; r2=0.74), moDC (DEND2; r2=0.91), and lipid-handling macrophages (MAC1, r2=0.87) across diverse experimental conditions.
source: We found that ASC1 proliferation and differentiation were strongly predicted by the magnitude of cold-induced recruitment of cDC1 (DEND1; r2=0.74), moDC (DEND2; r2=0.91), and lipid-handling macrophages (MAC1, r2=0.87) across these diverse experimental conditions (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from correlation analysis across multiple experiments shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The highly significant relationship between ASC1 proliferation/differentiation and immune cell recruitment held even when basal values were excluded from the analysis.
source: Importantly, this highly significant relationship held even when basal values were excluded from the analysis.
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis.

claim: MAC2 are the predominant macrophage subtype of control (RT) mice and their levels sharply declined during cold exposure.
source: MAC2 are the predominant macrophage subtype of control (RT) mice and their levels sharply declined during cold exposure (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: MAC2 express F4/80 (Adgre1) and MHCII (H2-Ab1), have a compact morphology, and are evenly distributed throughout the parenchyma.
source: MAC2 express F4/80 (Adgre1) and MHCII (H2-Ab1), have a compact morphology, and are evenly distributed throughout the parenchyma (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a finding from the immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Cold exposure led to the dramatic appearance of GPNMB+ MAC1 cells and dendritic cells labeled with MHCII antibodies.
source: Histological analysis of iBAT at the peak for cold-induced proliferation demonstrated the dramatic appearance of GPNMB+ MAC1 cells and dendritic cells labeled with MHCII antibodies (noting that MHCII+ MAC2 are nearly absent in iBAT of cold-exposed mice; Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a finding from the immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Nearly all MAC1 and dendritic cells were present in clusters in two distinct locations: within 50 micrometers of the tissue border or near acellular vacancies in the parenchyma.
source: Interestingly, nearly all MAC1 and dendritic cells were present in clusters in two distinct locations: within 50 micrometers of the tissue border or near acellular vacancies in the parenchyma.
evidence: This is a finding from the immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: Nearly all actively proliferating ASC1 (MKI67+ PDGFRA+) cells were in close proximity to F4/80+ immune cells.
source: High-resolution confocal imaging of the tissue border region demonstrated that nearly all actively proliferating ASC1 (MKI67+ PDGFRA+) cells were in close proximity to F4/80+ immune cells (Figure 7B and Appendix 1—Video 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the high-resolution confocal imaging shown in Figure 7B.

claim: ASC1 cellular processes extend toward and contact F4/80+ cells.
source: 3-D confocal microscopy of cold-exposed iBAT indicates that ASC1 cellular processes extend toward and contact F4/80+ cells (Figure 7B and Appendix 1—Video 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the 3-D confocal microscopy shown in Figure 7B.

claim: GPNMB+ MAC1 and MHCII+ dendritic cells were observed surrounding vacancies lacking cellular autofluorescence and PLIN1.
source: We also observed GPNMB+ MAC1 and MHCII+ dendritic cells surrounding vacancies lacking cellular autofluorescence and PLIN1, a lipid droplet marker of live adipocytes (Figure 7C and Appendix 1—Video 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The vacancies appear to be sites of efferocytosis by GPNMB+ MAC1 and MHCII+ dendritic cells.
source: Thus, the vacancies appear to be sites of efferocytosis by GPNMB+ MAC1 and MHCII+ dendritic cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the immunofluorescence observations.

claim: Sites of efferocytosis contained actively proliferating (MKI67+) ASC1 (PDGFRA+) near immune cells (F4/80+).
source: Importantly, these sites contained actively proliferating (MKI67+) ASC1 (PDGFRA+) near immune cells (F4/80+) (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a finding from the immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Proliferating progenitors were closely associated with H2-Ab1+ dendritic cells.
source: As expected from immunofluorescence analysis (Figure 8A–B), proliferating progenitors and differentiating adipocytes were nearest neighbors (NN) of themselves, reflecting clustering within adipogenic niches. Furthermore, proliferating progenitors were closely associated with H2-Ab1+ dendritic cells (Figure 8A) and this close association declined by four- to five-fold as progenitors differentiated into BAs (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a finding from the smFISH analysis shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The close association between proliferating progenitors and H2-Ab1+ dendritic cells declined by four- to five-fold as progenitors differentiated into BAs.
source: Furthermore, proliferating progenitors were closely associated with H2-Ab1+ dendritic cells (Figure 8A) and this close association declined by four- to five-fold as progenitors differentiated into BAs (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a finding from the smFISH analysis shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Progenitor proliferation occurs in close proximity to recruited immune cells, which depart as progenitors differentiate into BAs.
source: These data indicate that progenitor proliferation occurs in close proximity to recruited immune cells, which depart as progenitors differentiate into BAs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the smFISH analysis.

claim: MHCII+ DC were three times more likely to be within 10 micrometers of a dividing preadipocyte versus a divided/differentiated brown adipocyte.
source: This analysis indicated that MHCII+ DC were three times more likely to be with 10 micrometers of a dividing preadipocyte versus a divided/differentiated brown adipocyte (27.3% vs 9.35%, p=0.00013, n=267 cells, 2–3 mice) (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the EdU labeling and immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Nearly all progenitors that divided on day 3, yet failed to differentiate by day 5, maintained close contact with MHCII+ cells in the tissue microenvironment.
source: In this experiment, we also located a limited number of progenitors that divided on day 3, yet failed to differentiate by day 5, and found that nearly all of these cells maintained close contact with MHCII+ cells in the tissue microenvironment (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the EdU labeling and immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: ASC1 and recruited immune cells comprise a cellular niche for progenitor proliferation and immune cells depart the niche as progenitors differentiate into BAs.
source: Taken together, these observations indicate that ASC1 and recruited immune cells comprise a cellular niche for progenitor proliferation and that immune cells depart the niche as progenitors differentiate into BAs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the spatial analysis data.

claim: Osteopontin (Spp1) is known to be chemotactic for ASCs in other adipose depots.
source: Osteopontin (Spp1), a DEG in the cold-induced MAC1 cluster (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), is known to be chemotactic for ASCs in other adipose depots (Lee et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2012.

claim: Cd44 and Sdc1 were identified as receptors for Spp1.
source: Cd44 molecule (Cd44) and Syndecan 1 (Sdc1) were identified as receptors for Spp1 in our queried databases (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is a finding from the ligand-receptor analysis shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Cd44 has been identified as a marker of activated adipocyte progenitors in other depots.
source: Cd44 has already been identified as a marker of activated adipocyte progenitors in other depots (Lee et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2013a; Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2013a; Lee et al., 2014.

claim: Sdc1 has been categorized as a regulator of adipogenesis.
source: Sdc1 has been categorized as a regulator of adipogenesis (Gougoula et al., 2019; Yu et al., 2020; Zaragosi et al., 2015), and its expression was highly specific to the cold-activated ASC1 cells.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gougoula et al., 2019; Yu et al., 2020; Zaragosi et al., 2015.

claim: Cold exposure greatly upregulated ASC1 expression of Adam12.
source: In this regard, cold exposure greatly upregulated ASC1 expression of the disintegrin and metalloproteinase ADAM metallopeptidase domain 12 (Adam12; Figure 9B).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 9B.

claim: ADAM12 is a multifunctional sheddase that could promote ASC1 proliferation and differentiation by multiple mechanisms, including local release of active HB-EGF and augmentation of IGF1 signaling via inactivation of IGFBP3.
source: ADAM12 is multifunctional sheddase that could promote ASC1 proliferation and differentiation by multiple mechanisms, including local release of active HB-EGF and augmentation of IGF1 signaling via inactivation of IGFBP3 (Taylor et al., 2014; Loechel et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Taylor et al., 2014; Loechel et al., 2000.

claim: ADAM12 promotes adipogenesis in vitro.
source: Indeed, ADAM12 promotes adipogenesis in vitro, and ectopic overexpression of ADAM12 in muscle is sufficient to induce fat pad formation in vivo (Coles et al., 2018; Kawaguchi et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Coles et al., 2018; Kawaguchi et al., 2002.

claim: Ectopic overexpression of ADAM12 in muscle is sufficient to induce fat pad formation in vivo.
source: Indeed, ADAM12 promotes adipogenesis in vitro, and ectopic overexpression of ADAM12 in muscle is sufficient to induce fat pad formation in vivo (Coles et al., 2018; Kawaguchi et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Coles et al., 2018; Kawaguchi et al., 2002.

claim: 100% (258/258, n=5 mice) of new brown adipocytes were derived from the proliferation of cells with a recent history of Pdgfra expression.
source: In further support of this conclusion, we repeated the lineage tracing experiments described in Lee et al., 2015 using an independent Pdgfra-CreERT2 x LSL-tdTomato mouse model and found that 100% (258/258, n=5 mice) of new brown adipocytes were derived from the proliferation of cells with a recent history of Pdgfra expression.
evidence: This is a finding from the lineage tracing experiments.

claim: Myf5 expression was not present/expressed in any adult stromal cell subtype.
source: Although Myf5 expression has been linked to development of the BA lineage (Lee et al., 2015; Seale et al., 2008), it was not present/expressed in any adult stromal cell subtype.
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: Pdgfra+ ASC1 cells are the immediate progenitors of cold-induced BAs in adult iBAT.
source: Rather, our scRNA-seq data clearly demonstrate that Pdgfra+ ASC1 cells are the immediate progenitors of cold-induced BAs in adult iBAT.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the scRNA-seq data.

claim: Cold-induced neogenesis is largely an indirect response to chronic activation of BAs that ultimately serves to increase thermogenic capacity to match thermogenic demand.
source: Together, these results indicate that cold-induced neogenesis is largely an indirect response to chronic activation of BAs that ultimately serves to increase thermogenic capacity to match thermogenic demand.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.
